species.label: Bluefin tuna
species.note: Sport-fleet catch peaks at 63-70°F (Runcie 2019); in warmer surface water bluefin go deep, out of reach of surface gear.

species.label: Yellowfin tuna
species.note: Holds on the warm, clear side of fronts (Block 1997); a shallow mixed layer pushes it up.

species.label: Dorado (mahi)
species.note: The paddy fish: 75% of Mexican Pacific catch at chlorophyll 0.05-0.25 mg/m³ (Marín-Enríquez 2018).

species.label: Yellowtail (offshore, paddy fish)
species.note: San Diego catch rates rise at 64-68°F and fall above 69°F (Squire 1982; inshore fleet data).

species.label: Striped marlin
species.note: San Diego catch averaged 67.8°F; works breaks and blue water against green over the banks.

species.label: Wahoo
species.note: A warm-year visitor (CPFV: 42 in 2014, 256 in 2015); holds on banks and high spots.

fleet_recent.coverage_note: AIS is heard only within roughly 30-50 nm of shore receivers, and most boats under 65 ft never broadcast it.

inshore.label: Yellowtail (islands and kelp)
inshore.drivers: Warm-year regime (landings swing from under 10,000 to 450,000 fish), bait: squid, sardine, mackerel.
inshore.look: Outer kelp edge next to deep water, up-current points at the islands.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the regime; the 64-66°F 'switch' is angler lore.
inshore.today: Surface water is 75°F; San Diego catch rates have fallen above 69°F in fleet data.

inshore.label: White seabass
inshore.drivers: Spawning Mar-Jul (peak May); tagged fish spent half their time at 55-61°F, tracking the thermocline.
inshore.look: Kelp near squid grounds, at dusk; near the surface Apr-Oct, deeper Dec-Feb.
inshore.evidence: Thermal niche from one tagging study (Aalbers & Sepulveda 2015).
inshore.today: Surface water is 75°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 177 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it.

inshore.label: Calico (kelp) bass
inshore.drivers: Small home ranges; spawns Jun-Aug at 25-60 ft under kelp.

inshore.label: Market squid (the bait that drives the inshore bite)
inshore.drivers: Landings crash after big El Niños; eggs at 50-58°F.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the El Niño effect: a weak squid year is likely this winter.

fishing.method: Profiles say where the water matches what each species needs, not how many fish are there. Water temperature is the satellite map's; breaks are the strongest gradient within 10 nm of a spot, read as the temperature change across 4.3 nm. A cue met at most in-range spots that day is 'everywhere' and singles nothing out.
fishing.counts_note: No dock counts: the network that publishes SoCal landing counts now forbids automated collection and republishing without a license.

bottom_line: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove, La Jolla Shores, Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs, and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 2 to 4 feet from 210°, with a moderate rip current risk.

By boat today: marginal for the Coronados; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore, the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands. Monday gets worse for San Diego inshore, the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands (steep short-period chop, NWS advisories and wind).
Nearshore buoys read 74-76°F as of 5:26 PM; the latest satellite temperature map is from Oct 23.

fishing: By boat today: marginal for the Coronados; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore, the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands. Monday gets worse for San Diego inshore, the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands (steep short-period chop, NWS advisories and wind).
Water at the named spots runs 67-75°F on the Oct 23 satellite map; the strongest break is near San Clemente Island, 1.9°F over 4.3 nm, warm side to the E.
Season and water both match today for bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, dorado, yellowtail, striped marlin and wahoo. That says the water is right, not that fish are there.
AIS shows 9 boats at sea in the last 3 hours. Over the last three days the fleet stopped longest at 33.65N 118.17W.
diving: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove, La Jolla Shores, Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs, and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 2 to 4 feet from 210°, with a moderate rip current risk.
No shore entry is within or marginal on our thresholds today. Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 10-15 ft at San Diego on Oct 22.

Suit: 3-5 mm for most divers, sized for 72°F at 60 ft in the nearest glider profile. Kelp-bed bottoms can run colder when internal tides push cold water in. A glider 63 nm from San Diego measured 72°F at the surface and 70°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 177 ft (1:38 PM Oct 25).
spearfishing: Entries today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove, La Jolla Shores, Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs, and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 2 to 4 feet from 210°, with a moderate rip current risk.
Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 10-15 ft at San Diego on Oct 22: enough to hunt pelagics (15 ft or more).

A glider 63 nm from San Diego measured 72°F at the surface and 70°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 177 ft (1:38 PM Oct 25). White seabass: Surface water is 75°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 177 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it. Open now: spiny lobster (by hand only).

synopsis.text: At 12 PM, a 1025 mb high was 700 nautical miles west of San Francisco, CA and a 1012 mb low was over east central Nevada. Weak offshore flow near shore during the nights and mornings will alternate with onshore northwest flow during the afternoons and evenings through Tuesday. Stronger onshore winds Monday afternoon and evening may gust to 20 knots. More steady onshore flow expected from Wednesday onwards.
At 18Z or 11 AM PDT, a 1022 mb high was 500 NM west of Monterey, California.

headlines.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
morning hours.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents in the warned area should
be alert for rising water and take appropriate action to protect
life and property. High tides each day will occur in the
morning. Tides may be anywhere from 1 to 1.7 feet above
astronomical tide predictions.
headlines.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth. Stay off of jetties and sea walls. Avoid
beaches during high tides. During high and rising tides, waves
may run farther up the beach than expected. Stay far back from the
water and never turn your back on the ocean.
